subject: psychology
title: Social Influence: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Evaluate Milgram and apply social influence to real-world scenarios.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology exam stretch on social influence: evaluation, ethics and application to crowds.
final_note: You can evaluate classic studies on ethical and methodological grounds.

concepts.def: Concerns about harm, consent and deception.

walkthroughs.body_html: Milgram is criticised for deception, lack of fully informed consent and psychological harm. He defended the study with thorough debriefing and a follow-up survey: most participants said they were glad to have taken part.

walkthroughs.h2: Asch: a child of its time?
walkthroughs.body_html: Perrin & Spencer (1980) repeated Asch in the UK and found almost no conformity in engineering students. This suggests Asch's high conformity reflected 1950s US culture and limits the study's temporal validity.

'A man collapses on a busy street and nobody helps.' Explain using diffusion of responsibility and pluralistic ignorance. Suggest one way to reduce the bystander effect, e.g. naming a specific person to call 999.
